description_html:
In the Combinatorial Auction (CA) problem, \(n\) bids \((B_i, p_i)\) for subsets of \(m\) items are given, where \(B_i\) is the subset (bundle) of items requested by bid \(i\) and \(p_i\) is its bidding price. The objective is to accept a set of pairwise compatible bids (no item is sold twice) that maximizes the total revenue.

All instances in this library are generated with the arbitrary relationships scheme of [Leyton-Brown00] (Section 4.3), using the generator of [Gasse19] (very easy, easy and medium levels; the very hard levels of [Huang23] use the same generator with 2,000/4,000 items and 4,000/8,000 bids). Each bidder submits an initial bundle (built by adding items one by one with probability 0.7, guided by the bidder's private interests and pairwise item compatibilities) together with up to 5 substitutable bundles that share at least one item with the initial one, i.e. at most 6 bids per bidder. A bundle's price is the sum of the bidder's private item values (common resale value drawn uniformly from \([1,100]\), perturbed by up to \(\pm 50\)) plus a super-additive term \(|B_i|^{1.2}\); prices are real-valued. A bidder's bids are mutually exclusive (XOR bids). When a bidder places 3 or more bids, the generator encodes this exclusivity with a dummy item that is added to all of that bidder's bundles; bidders with exactly 2 bids need no dummy item because a substitutable bundle always shares an item with the initial bundle. The regions distribution of [Leyton-Brown00] is not used here.

Notation.

  • \(N=\{1,\dots,n\}\): bids; \(p_i>0\): price of bid \(i\in N\).
  • \(M=\{1,\dots,m\}\): items; \(B_i\subseteq M\): items requested by bid \(i\).
  • \(M^+=\{j\in M: \exists i\in N,\ j\in B_i\}\): items requested by at least one bid (items nobody bids on yield no constraint).
  • \(K\): bidders that placed at least 3 bids (one dummy item each); \(N_k\subseteq N\): the bids of bidder \(k\in K\) (\(3\le |N_k|\le 6\)).
  • \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\): 1 if bid \(i\) is accepted.

Formulation.

\begin{align} \max\ & \sum_{i\in N} p_i x_i \\ \textrm{s.t.}\ & \sum_{i\in N:\, j\in B_i} x_i \leq 1, && \forall j\in M^+, \\ & \sum_{i\in N_k} x_i \leq 1, && \forall k\in K, \\ & x_i\in\{0,1\}, && \forall i\in N. \end{align}

The second family is the item constraint of the dummy items, so in the files every constraint has the same form \(\sum_{i: j\in B_i} x_i\le 1\) over the extended item set \(M^+\cup K\), and the number of constraints is \(|M^+|+|K|\). This is why the constraint count exceeds the number of items (e.g. about 192 constraints for 100 items: roughly 100 item rows plus about 90 dummy-item rows).
changes: Formulation now includes the bidder-exclusivity (XOR) constraints that the generator encodes as dummy items; the old formulation had only one row per real item and could not explain constraint counts (e.g. 192.2 rows for 100 items).
Item constraints are indexed by items that receive at least one bid (M^+); items without bids produce no row (observed: 199/200 items used in CA easy test_0, ~1,932/2,000 in very-hard).

Prose: replaced 'two commonly used distributions: regions and arbitrary' by the fact that all levels use the arbitrary scheme, plus a short description of the generator (add_item_prob 0.7, up to 5 substitutable bids, prices = private values + |B|^1.2, real-valued).
Notation list added. Added a 'Bid Distribution' column (Arbitrary for all levels). #Item/#Bid values unchanged (confirmed).
verification: Generator: ds4dm/learn2branch 01_generate_instances.py generate_cauctions(..., add_item_prob=0.7); levels 100/500 (train), 200/1000, 300/1500 (transfer). Very-hard: local generator_MVC_MIS_CA_SC_MK.py (same function, add_item_prob=0.7, n_items=2000, n_bids=4000) and Huang23 Sec. 5 ('2,000 items and 4,000 bids according to the arbitrary relations').

CA/easy test 0,1: 1000 binaries, 375 / 382 rows (table avg 385.04), all rows '<= 1' with unit coefficients, maximize, real-valued prices 3.7..1457. Row split (rows are written item order then dummy order): 199 + 176 dummy, 200 + 182 dummy. Dummy rows are disjoint blocks of 3-6 consecutive bids, as the generator produces.
CA/very-hard test 0,1: 4000 binaries, 2669 / 2680 rows (table 2676.32; Huang23 Table 1: 2,675): 1933+736, 1931+749 (some of the 2,000 items receive no bid).

Very easy (100/500) and Very hard 2 (4,000/8,000) are not on Hugging Face; values come from the current table, Gasse19 and Huang23 Table 1 (CA-L: 8,000 vars, 5,353 constraints). Their constraint counts fit the same item+dummy structure.
open_questions: The split of rows into real-item vs dummy-item rows was inferred (dummy rows are trailing disjoint blocks of 3-6 consecutive bids); a real-item row that happens to be such a block could be misclassified, so counts of used items are approximate (+-1).
